summary: Recovered `/srv/archive` online. Removed the unexpected 690,073,600-byte telemetry debug capture, reducing utilization from 100% to 7%. Existing archive data was preserved, archiveapp can write successfully, and all results persisted through the required node restart.
actions_performed: Identified `/srv/archive/.telemetry-cache/collector-debug.capture` as the unexpected space consumer.
Removed only the debug capture and its empty cache directory.
Verified the archive manifest checksum and content remained unchanged.
Verified archiveapp can write, read, and delete probe files in `/srv/archive/incoming`.
Safely restarted node1 and verified its boot identity changed, the system recovered, the XFS archive mounted read-write, utilization remained 7%, and archive data and write capability persisted.

evidence.summary: Shows the root-owned 690,073,600-byte debug capture consumed nearly the entire filesystem while the archive manifest was intact.

evidence.requirement: Bring /srv/archive below 80% without taking the server offline
evidence.summary: Utilization changed from 100% to 7% after targeted removal while the XFS filesystem remained mounted.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the filesystem and existing archive data
evidence.summary: The XFS mount remained read-write and the archive manifest retained checksum c27a3936f654dcb08a389ac6bb44555e46c91969e8f7767490f219e83f0c009 before cleanup, after cleanup, and after restart.
The initial probe failed with ENOSPC; post-cleanup and post-restart write/read/delete probes both succeeded.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 83a0a80f-773c-4f3e-9137-1e7aa887b07a; reboot scheduling was acknowledged; node1 returned with boot ID 9b5d5c32-753c-4bdd-bab1-bbb9e9d68869 and system state running; final checks proved the archive mount, data, capacity, and archiveapp writes recovered.
